title: bridge-executor: multi-tool shuttle with temporal sentinels and injection anchoring
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement and stabilize a new executor variant (bridge-executor) that routes a single API request through a configurable sequence of tools/functions while preserving streaming semantics and structured outputs. Key goals: safe result injection between tools, deterministic anchoring of injected tokens into the ongoing response stream, and robust recursion/loop detection with measurable fallbacks. This is intended to enable orchestrated multi-tool flows (e.g., fetch -> transform -> external-call -> summarize) without introducing silent infinite loops or streaming breaks for clients.
acceptance_criteria: Bridge-executor accepts a declarative step list and preserves streaming backpressure to the client during tool invocation and result injection
Injected results must be anchored with idempotency tokens and KV anchors so downstream steps can reference them reliably
Recursion/loop safeguards detect cycles within 5 iterations or 3s per-request time window and trigger a graceful fallback policy
Compatibility layer supports existing function-calling payloads and structured-output schemas (JSON schema + typed events) without breaking hosted customers
End-to-end tests covering streaming + tool injection across network interruptions and retries
Telemetry surfaces per-step latency, recursion sentinel firings, and injected-token lineage in Console dashboard
notes: Design rationale: current runner binds tool calls to synchronous phases which causes buffering and breaks client streaming. The bridge-executor will stitch partial outputs and stream them immediately while marking injected fragments so the client can rehydrate structured outputs.

We will use a small metadata envelope around injected fragments: {anchor_id, idempotency, source_step, ttl_ms}. Anchors are stored in the request-scoped KV cache for lifetime of request plus a short staleness window (default 15s).

Fallback policy options: 1) Abort with structured error plus last-good-output, 2) Replace offending step with preconfigured no-op model, 3) Return partial stream and mark downstream as degraded. Initial rollout uses option 3 for best availability.

Recursion detection heuristics considered: depth counter, repeated anchor reuse within a sliding window, semantically identical payload signature. We will implement a combined heuristic: iteration_count >= 5 OR repeated_anchor_hits >= 3 within 10s triggers sentinel.
Security review: injected payloads may include external-call results; they must be sanitized and redacted by the executor before being inserted into the stream unless the route has allowlist flag.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike): prototype streaming anchor envelopes and per-request KV anchors in a sandbox runtime (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (engine): integrate bridge-executor into runtime router, add idempotency token validation, and guardrails (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (compat): compatibility shim that converts existing function-calling JSON into envelope format and back (1 week)
Phase 4 (tests & telemetry): build E2E tests, add dashboard panels, set SLO alerts, and run canary on a subset of tenants (2 weeks)
Phase 5 (rollout): incremental rollouts with canary -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback on sentinel spike (1 week)
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Spike completed. Prototype successfully streams injected fragments from tool B into the client's ongoing response with <50ms additional latency in local env.
2026-02-20: Implemented anchor envelope format and per-request KV anchor store. Found race where concurrent tool invocations overwrote anchors; added per-anchor mutex and optimistic write-check.

2026-02-25: Hooked up recursion heuristic. Tuned thresholds after internal load tests — depth=5 produced false positives on long planned pipelines, adjusted to depth>=8 + repeated_anchor_hits>=3 within 12s.
2026-02-28: Compatibility shim pass completed. Existing function-calling SDKs can opt into envelope mode via 'bridge_compat=true' flag. PM requested default opt-in for new routes only.
2026-03-01: Started writing E2E tests for network interruption cases and streaming resume semantics.
comments: Sofia Gomez (PM) [2026-02-18]: Please ensure that console UI can surface which step produced each injected fragment — important for customer debuggability.
Ethan Liang (SRE) [2026-02-21]: We need to cap per-request KV memory usage. Proposal: limit anchor count to 50 per request and evict least-recently-used anchors when exceeded.
Design Review (2026-02-24): Reviewed anchor envelope fields and agreed to add an optional 'safety_policy' tag to allow conservative redaction on high-risk tenants.
Marco Chen (Assignee) [2026-02-26]: Implemented mutex for anchor writes and added metrics for anchor create/update/fetch. Uploading PR for internal review.
Security (2026-02-27): Recommend running sanitizer pass via transform tool rather than executor for better policy separation.
